benchmark_scope: Lygon Street and supplied-image venues are inspiration only and are not counted as Sydney competitors

competitors.name: Diego & Co.

price_observation_aud.basis: displayed schiacciate; excludes online platform service fee

competitors.positioning: Authentic Tuscan schiacciata within a short walk of Wynyard; high ingredient specificity and made-to-order lunch focus.
competitors.implication_for_buono: Sets a credible CBD sandwich ceiling around $25 and shows that proximity and speed can support premium imported deli fillings.

sources.title: Diego & Co. official menu and venue page

competitors.name: Delisia

price_observation_aud.basis: editorial observation at December 2024; current exact prices unknown

competitors.positioning: Small Italian-inspired café specialising in same-day baked focaccia and made-to-order deli sandwiches.
competitors.implication_for_buono: Confirms fresh focaccia as a destination product in a neighbourhood format, but the historic price point requires live menu recheck before modelling.

competitors.name: Good Ways Deli
competitors.location_archetype: inner-south neighbourhood and weekday worker catchment

price_observation_aud.basis: 2025 Broadsheet special only; full current menu is image-based and not captured

competitors.positioning: Cult-followed Sydney sandwich and bakery brand with a second site, house-baked rolls and nostalgic Australian flavours.
competitors.implication_for_buono: Shows that local identity and bakery capability can travel to a second neighbourhood. The absence of evening trade leaves whitespace for a true day-to-night model.

sources.title: Four Sandwich Specials Hitting Sydney Especially for Dine Out

competitors.name: Raineri's Continental Delicatessen
competitors.role: direct Sydney benchmark with incomplete primary evidence
competitors.location: 97 Great North Road, Five Dock NSW 2046

price_observation_aud.basis: reported 2026 sandwich price in secondary coverage; primary menu unavailable

competitors.positioning: Long-running family deli whose fresh focaccia sandwiches have become a social-media-driven destination.
competitors.implication_for_buono: Queue reports are a useful demand signal for heritage plus abundance, but they do not prove durable repeat demand or service throughput.

sources.title: Why hundreds of Aussies are lining up outside this tiny Sydney deli

competitors.name: IL BARETTO Newtown

price_observation_aud.basis: pasta menu; focaccia $6, salad $12, takeaway bundles $29-$79, spritz $18

competitors.positioning: Old-school pasta bar relaunched as a high-energy takeaway and dine-in ritual with pasta boxes, focaccia, tiramisu and wine.
competitors.implication_for_buono: Directly validates the proposed category stack and King Street geography. Buono must differentiate through morning trade, salad strength, heritage narrative and a tighter six-six-six system.

sources.title: IL BARETTO Newtown, Pasta, Focaccia & Tiramisu

competitors.name: The Italian Bowl
competitors.role: direct Sydney pasta and salad competitor
competitors.positioning: Visible pan-to-bowl preparation, broad choose-pasta/choose-sauce menu, generous portions and walk-in accessibility.
competitors.implication_for_buono: Confirms demand for bowl language and theatre, but the very broad menu creates an opening for a shorter, more legible offer.

competitors.name: Fabbrica Pasta Shop CBD
competitors.location_archetype: CBD office, retail and evening catchment

price_observation_aud.basis: same sandwich takeaway versus dine-in with pickles and side

competitors.positioning: Design-led pasta factory, deli, sandwich shop and low-intervention wine store that carries one footprint across retail and hospitality.
competitors.implication_for_buono: Strong precedent for production theatre and day-to-night asset utilisation. Also proves that format pricing can distinguish takeaway from dine-in value.

competitors.name: FISHBOWL
competitors.location: 18 named Greater Sydney markets; 50+ Australian locations
competitors.location_archetype: CBD, beach, neighbourhood and shopping-centre network
competitors.hours_observed: Most locations open from 11am; site-specific closing times vary
competitors.positioning: Fast, healthy, made-to-order bowl platform with strong design, customisation and a wide network.
competitors.implication_for_buono: This is the reference price and convenience competitor for salads. Buono salads need to feel like complete meals, with fast assembly and credible protein, at a comparable sub-$22 ceiling for core versions.

competitors.name: Bar Allora
competitors.role: direct Sydney day-to-night and aperitivo competitor
competitors.location: 2 Bond Street, corner George Street, Sydney NSW 2000

price_observation_aud.basis: $10 aperitivo beer/wine, $15 spritz/negroni, $25 express lunch; standing espresso $1.50

competitors.positioning: Unapologetically Italian from morning espresso to late drinks, using strong daypart-specific offers.
competitors.implication_for_buono: Closest proof of daypart switching in the CBD. Its discount windows show that transition periods may need a sharp, explicit ritual rather than passive menu availability.

competitors.name: Bloom Potts Point
competitors.hours_observed: Cafe Wed-Fri 11am-3pm and Sat-Sun 8am-3pm; bar/restaurant Wed-Sat 3pm-10pm

price_observation_aud.basis: aperitivo menu: small plates $6-$18, panino $17, pasta $28, platter $39; drinks $7-$14

competitors.positioning: Explicit café-by-day, aperitivo-by-dusk, restaurant-by-night conversion with in-house bread, focaccia and pasta.
competitors.implication_for_buono: Validates the exact operating architecture but also demonstrates higher eastern-suburbs menu pricing. It should be treated as a direct model comparator, not proof that every Sydney catchment will support the same basket.

interstate_benchmarks.sydney_status: not a Sydney competitor; South Australian network with a Hawthorn, Victoria venue

price_observation_aud.basis: January 2026 displayed regular/large examples before some premium pasta upgrades

interstate_benchmarks.benchmark_value: Compact service theatre, highly legible choice architecture and accessible pasta pricing.

interstate_benchmarks.name: Sangaweech
interstate_benchmarks.sydney_status: not a Sydney competitor; Lygon Street, Carlton benchmark

price_observation_aud.basis: current accessible price evidence not established

interstate_benchmarks.benchmark_value: Single-product naming, nostalgic Italian-Australian cues and a compact frontage.

interstate_benchmarks.name: Johnny, Vince & Sam's
interstate_benchmarks.sydney_status: not a Sydney competitor; 306-308 Lygon Street, Carlton

price_observation_aud.basis: July 2024 menu, including $18 spritz and pasta about $27-$34; 2026 currency unknown

interstate_benchmarks.benchmark_value: High-energy heritage storytelling and convivial evening trade on Lygon Street.

interstate_benchmarks.name: Hector's Deli
interstate_benchmarks.sydney_status: not a Sydney competitor; Melbourne network

price_observation_aud.basis: current sandwiches; salad $18, breakfast egg and cheese $7.50

interstate_benchmarks.benchmark_value: Short menu, strong product photography, production-line counter and replicable 7am-3pm format across multiple site types.

competitive_gaps.claim: No reviewed Sydney venue combines a disciplined six-pasta, six-focaccia, six-salad menu with full morning-to-late operation exactly as proposed.
competitive_gaps.caveat: This is based on the reviewed set, not an exhaustive census of every Sydney venue.

sources.title: IL BARETTO Newtown, Pasta, Focaccia & Tiramisu

competitive_gaps.claim: The strongest whitespace is not an unserved cuisine. It is a simpler, faster, all-day Italian neighbourhood system that gives salads equal status and converts deliberately into aperitivo.
